# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 63 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 63 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_063_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 6, Part 1 — The Shepherd of Luxury

**63:1** As I was sitting at home and glorifying God for all the things I had seen, and thinking over the commandments how they were beautiful and powerful and glad and glorious and able to save the soul of a man, I said within myself: I shall be blessed if I walk in these commandments, and whoever walks in them shall be blessed.

**63:2** As I was saying these things within myself, I saw him sitting beside me and saying: "Why are you double-minded about the commandments which I gave you? They are beautiful. Have no doubt at all, but clothe yourself with the faith of the Lord and you shall walk in them. For I will strengthen you in them."

**63:3** "This commandment is especially welcome to me, lord," I said, "because I have never in my life sinned against it." "Speak," he said. "I have always," I said, "even to this day, kept myself pure from women, from every kind of adultery and impurity." And he rejoiced at this and said: "Good; you say this because you have not sinned. But I will tell you something else. You must guard the flesh holy and undefiled, so that the Spirit which dwells in it may bear testimony to it, and your flesh may be justified."

**63:4** "Be careful," he said, "lest any thought enter into your heart concerning this flesh of yours and you consider it defiled. For if the pure flesh is defiled by an evil thought, it works death. But keep it pure and believe that if you keep the flesh pure, you shall live to God."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the transition to Similitude 6 and the flesh-purity instruction.*
